title: Solar Grain Mills — Soroti, Serere & Kaberamaido
summary: Solar-powered grain milling facilities replacing diesel mills in three adjacent districts of Teso sub-region, Eastern Uganda.
description: Grain milling in the Teso sub-region of Eastern Uganda relies heavily on diesel-powered mills. Fuel costs account for up to 35% of milling service costs, making milling unaffordable for the poorest households. This project replaced 9 diesel mills across Soroti, Serere, and Kaberamaido Districts with solar-powered alternatives, each with battery backup for cloudy days. The mills process maize, sorghum, and millet. Solar mill operators received training in financial management, and a revolving savings scheme was established at each site to fund maintenance and component replacement.
locationNote: Covers Soroti, Serere, and Kaberamaido Districts — Teso sub-region
fundingPartner: DFID Uganda Rural Energy Access Programme
outcomes: 9 diesel mills replaced; milling costs reduced 30%; 1,200 household-equivalent access; savings schemes operational at 7 sites.
